problems.title: The transformed Pareto variable need not have skewness two
problems.source_location: Proposition 1, p.4; Appendix A, p.21, Eq.7 and densities.
claim: Proposition 1 assigns skewness \(2\) to \(\log(1+T)\) for a standard Pareto time difference.
analysis: For standard Type-I Pareto \(T\) with shape \(\alpha\) and minimum \(c>0\), the density of \(Y=\log(1+T)\) is \[f_Y(y)=\frac{\alpha c^\alpha e^y}{(e^y-1)^{\alpha+1}},\qquad y\ge\log(1+c),\] rather than a shifted exponential density. With \(\alpha=4,c=1\), its first three moments are approximately \[(0.833333333333,0.718517562805,0.648490931824)\], giving skewness \(2.571420899\), rather than \(2\). More generally, write \(T=cV\) for \(V\sim\operatorname{Pareto}(1,\alpha)\), \(\alpha>3\). As \(c\downarrow0\), \(\log(1+cV)/c\to V\) and is bounded by \(V\). Dominated convergence of the first three moments implies its skewness approaches that of \(V\), which exceeds \(2\); it therefore cannot equal \(2\) for every scale. If the intended assumption is instead that \(1+T\) is Type-I Pareto, the shifted-exponential conclusion does hold.
result: The exact constant in current Proposition 1 is not valid for an arbitrary standard Type-I Pareto time difference. This is a distribution/shift condition issue; it does not refute empirical benefits of logarithmic compression or the paper’s acknowledged non-Pareto data behavior.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: State the appropriate shifted-Pareto/Lomax model or use the log-ratio transform.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Current Proposition 1, Appendix A and latest arXiv v1 retain the same shift and density. Specifying a Pareto law for the shifted variable is the existing conditional correction; the author’s intended convention remains unconfirmed.

problems.title: Equal-time memory can include non-past events
problems.source_location: Sections 3.1/3.3, PDF pp. 3–6; current models/modules.py, decoder forward/TRCMemory; evaluate_models_utils.py, positive-batch update
claim: The task definition predicts at \(\tau\) from the graph strictly before \(\tau\).
analysis: The current decoder retrieves memory by node pair without a query-time filter; positive-batch prediction then updates that memory. Consider two events for pair \((1,2)\), both at timestamp \(1\), in successive batches with initially empty memory. Set the current one-dimensional edge embedding to \(1\), the historical aggregation weight to \(1/2\), and the final logit to the stored historical coordinate. The first prediction has logit \(0\), then stores \(1/2\); the next same-time prediction reads logit \(1/2\), yielding probability \(\sigma(1/2)\approx0.6224593312\) rather than \(0.5\). Under the paper’s strict \(G_{<1}\) semantics, neither event is available to the other, so both should read empty historical memory. A strictly later query may legitimately read the first event, and events kept in one batch read the same pre-batch state. These controls isolate the equal-time batch boundary.
result: The current author release still permits this strict-time information mismatch. No current AP change, prediction change count or historical experiment contamination rate was measured. A protocol ordered by timestamp and event index could permit such reads, but would require a different declared information clock.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Score an entire timestamp group before insertion, or filter stored events strictly before each query time.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: The latest author decoder removed an unused timestamp argument but still has no timestamped memory lookup. Current evaluation updates positive memories after each batch. The existing strict-time-group alternative remains an analytic proposal, not an adopted or benchmark-verified correction.
